notes: Declarative registry of non-interactive agent CLIs used by scripts/agent_runner.py.
argv templates may contain the literal placeholder {prompt}. {model} is replaced by the model flag when a model is requested.
confidence records how the invocation shape is known, not whether the CLI is good:
documented  - non-interactive invocation is documented by the tool's own maintainers
community   - invocation shape is reported by users and should be verified before use
unverified  - shape is a best guess; verify with --dry-run and a trivial prompt first
Run 'agent_runner.py list-runtimes' to see which of these are installed on the current host.
The 'custom' adapter takes any command prefix via --command and is the universal escape hatch: it works for any agent that can read a prompt from argv or stdin.

claude.notes: Claude Code non-interactive. CLAUDECODE is cleared so the runner can be invoked from inside a Claude Code session.

copilot.notes: GitHub Copilot CLI non-interactive prompt mode.

crush.notes: Charm Crush non-interactive run mode. Verify argv shape before relying on it.

amp.notes: Sourcegraph Amp. -x is the execute flag. Verify before use; no model flag is assumed.

aider.notes: Aider is interactive by default; --yes plus --message is the non-interactive path. It mutates the working tree, so run it inside a disposable directory.

goose.notes: Block Goose run mode with a text task. Verify before use.

droid.notes: Factory Droid non-interactive exec mode. Verify before use.

plandex.notes: Plandex non-interactive exec mode. Verify before use.

fabric.notes: fabric -p may be read as --pattern rather than --prompt; this adapter uses the long form to avoid that ambiguity.

custom.notes: Any command prefix supplied via --command. The prompt is appended as the final argument. Use this for MCP hosts, API harnesses, in-house agents, or any runtime not listed above.
